policy: Original pages informed taxonomy, adult scale, lateral silhouette, armor, appendage layout and qualitative color boundaries only. No source pixels were sampled, traced, copied, redistributed or hotlinked.
taxonomyNote: The stable game identifier keeps the familiar Pygmy Cory trade name. The current combination is Gastrodermus pygmaeus (Knaack, 1966); Corydoras pygmaeus is the basionym and remains widespread in aquarium literature.

targetForm.name: adult normally pigmented Pygmy Cory
targetForm.definition: Gastrodermus pygmaeus with a miniature elongate armored body, short rounded snout, inferior mouth with barbels, continuous dark mid-lateral stripe, translucent fins and moderately forked caudal.

viewCoverage.side: Strong: two exact licensed live-fish file pages plus a peer-reviewed comparative diagnosis constrain the elongate silhouette, short snout, stripe and fins.
viewCoverage.front: Partial: an oblique exact file page constrains relative head width and barbel placement, but no verified orthographic frontal original was found.
viewCoverage.top: Partial: an oblique exact file page constrains the head-to-peduncle taper qualitatively, but no verified live whole-body orthographic dorsal original was found.
viewCoverage.bodyWidth: Moderate uncertainty: width is a conservative inference from oblique views and the shared armored-catfish plan, not a calibrated measurement.

referenceGradeRationale: Authoritative size and taxonomy, peer-reviewed comparative external morphology, and exact licensed lateral images strongly constrain species identity and side appearance. Orthographic front and top views remain unavailable, so width is explicitly inferred.
